general.title: General Settings
general.gpu_hint: Controls planetary and deep-sky stages. Deep Sky Expert mode can override this preference. Auto and Hybrid use the GPU only where scientific parity exists and continue on CPU when an algorithm requires it; GPU only is strict.
general.gpu_none: No compatible GPU — analysis and stacking use CPU (SIMD).
general.quality_policy_hint: Maximum revalidates ambiguous AP matches; it is the default and can take longer.
general.decode_hint: Auto measures software decoding and available video acceleration for each FFmpeg file. Strict hardware fails preflight if unsupported and stops on decode failure; it never silently falls back to software. SER always keeps its native reader.
general.tutorials_hint: Shown only once per workflow. You can replay them whenever you need.
general.tutorials_reset_message: Tutorials will appear once again when you enter each workflow.
general.purity_hint: Controls the automatic limiters that cap what each slider does. Protected avoids halos, limb ringing and blown highlights. Pure lets the slider win, at the cost of those artefacts possibly returning.
general.purity_balanced_warning: Limiters at 50%: more effect per slider, with moderate risk of halos on high-contrast edges.
general.purity_pure_warning: No limiters: dark rings on the limb, background worms and blown highlights may return on a full Moon or solar disk.

common.interactive_hint: Interactive tutorial: use the highlighted control when it applies, or press Next and move at your own pace.

step0.title: Welcome to Zenith Astro Stacker!
step0.content: This is a general overview of how the software works. You can move with Next, and in guided workflows use highlighted controls when the tutorial asks for them.

step1.title: Import Video
step1.content: Start here by importing your SER or AVI files to process them individually.

step2.title: Batch Mode
step2.content: Process multiple videos automatically with the same configuration.

step3.title: Create Mosaic
step3.content: Join multiple lunar or solar panels into a single high-resolution image.

step4.title: Settings
step4.content: Adjust language and tutorial preferences here.

step5.title: Check for Updates
step5.content: Click here to search for new versions of the software and keep it up to date.

step0.title: Step 1: Import Video
step0.content: Start by selecting a .SER or .AVI video to process.

step1.title: Target Type
step1.content:
Choose the workflow language that best describes your capture.
Surface: Moon, Sun, or wide-detail scenes.
Planet / Lunar Phase: compact objects with a cleaner background.

step2.title: Step 2: Start Analysis
step2.content: Press this button now! to begin analyzing all frames. The system will evaluate the quality of each frame automatically.

step3.title: Preparing Analysis
step3.content: The system is starting the frame analysis. Please wait a moment while the data is processed.

step4.title: Step 3: Frame Selection
step4.content: Adjust the percentage of the best frames to stack. More frames = less noise, but includes lower quality frames.

step5.title: Step 4: Stacking Options
step5.content: Here you adjust Drizzle, Double-Pass Alignment, and Sharpening. Keep them conservative when you want a clean reference before fine post-processing.

step6.title: Step 5: Smart AP
step6.content: The Smart AP Generator creates the alignment mesh. Adjust AP Size and Threshold if you need finer points or more selective detection.

step7.title: Viewer: Source
step7.content: Before stacking, review the reference frame and alignment-point mesh here. This helps confirm that the system is tracking the right areas.

step8.title: Step 6: Start Stacking
step8.content: Once parameters are set and the source view looks right, press this button to begin stacking.

step9.title: Processing Details
step9.content: This card summarizes the stack: time, frames used, engine, AP points, throughput, and system details. Use it to validate that the process behaved as expected.

step10.title: Viewer: Result
step10.content: This is your stacked image. You can zoom and pan to inspect the details.

step11.title: Wavelets and Processing
step11.content: Adjust wavelets, deconvolution, color, and denoise from this card. Keep the Processed Result visible on the right so you can judge each change before continuing.

step12.title: Export Result
step12.content: Finally, save your processed image. You have options to export in PNG (8-bit) for general use or TIFF (16-bit) to preserve maximum quality.

step0.title: Batch Mode
step0.content: Use this workflow when you want to process several videos with the same calibration. First, select the folder that contains your captures.

step1.title: Batch Panel
step1.content: Here you will see the folder, the number of videos found, and the batch stages. This panel guides the workflow through final execution.

step2.title: Batch Target Type
step2.content: Choose whether the whole batch is Surface or Planet / Lunar Phase. This sets the analysis and alignment engine for every file.

step3.title: Batch Reference
step3.content: Load the first video to calibrate analysis, stacking, and post-processing. That setup becomes the template for the rest of the batch.

step4.title: Analyze Reference
step4.content: Run analysis on the reference video. The system measures quality, stability, and the data needed to repeat the workflow.

step5.title: Frame Selection
step5.content: Adjust the percentage of best frames. This value is used as the base for every video in the batch.

step6.title: Stacking Options
step6.content: Review Drizzle, Double-Pass Alignment, Normalize Colors, and Sharpening. These settings become the base recipe for the batch.

step7.title: Batch Smart AP
step7.content: Set AP Size and Threshold, then generate the Smart AP mesh. This helps the reference track the right detail before the recipe is repeated.

step8.title: Viewer: Source
step8.content: Review the reference and generated mesh here. Confirm that points cover useful areas before stacking.

step9.title: Stack Reference
step9.content: Stack the reference to validate the result before applying the same recipe to the full batch.

step10.title: Processing Details
step10.content: This card summarizes the reference stack: time, frames used, engine, AP points, throughput, and technical details.

step11.title: Post-Processing
step11.content: Adjust wavelets, deconvolution, color, and denoise on the reference while checking the Processed Result. These values will be replicated across every video.

step12.title: Batch Control
step12.content: Return to the batch panel to review completed stages and confirm the reference is ready as the template.

step13.title: Start Full Batch
step13.content: When the reference looks right, start the full batch. The system applies the validated configuration to the remaining files.

step14.title: Animation Editor
step14.content: When processing finishes, results move to the animation editor so you can review frames, reject bad ones, and export the final video.

step0.title: Mosaic Mode
step0.content: Use this workflow to join lunar or solar panels. You can work with videos that will be stacked first or with already processed images.

step1.title: Mosaic Sources
step1.content: Select the videos or images that will form the mosaic. Keep panels from the same session together to make stitching easier.

step2.title: Auto-Organize
step2.content: Press Auto-Organize so the system can place panels in the source viewer and you can review the initial layout.

step3.title: Source View
step3.content: Here you can inspect how the tiles were arranged before analysis, stacking, or final stitching.

step4.title: Global Analysis
step4.content: Analyze all panels to measure quality and prepare a consistent result. Wait for this to finish before continuing.

step5.title: Mosaic Process
step5.content: If you are working with videos, set the stacking percentage here and stack every tile before stitching.

step6.title: Guided Mode and Creation
step6.content: Create the final mosaic here. You can enable Guided Mode when you want your manual placement to have priority, but the recommended path is leaving it off so automatic stitching can find matches on its own. Press Create Mosaic and wait for it to finish.

step7.title: Step 6: Save or Process
step7.content: Mosaic completed! You can save as PNG/TIFF or send it to Wavelets for additional processing.

batch-scan.title: Set the batch scope

batch-load.title: Prepare the batch reference
batch-load.message: {{itemCount}} videos detected. Tune one representative video and Zenith will reuse that traceable recipe.

batch-analyze.title: Analyze the reference
batch-analyze.message: The reference sets quality, mesh and percentage for the whole batch. Make sure it represents the session well.

batch-run.title: The batch recipe is ready
batch-run.message: Review the output folder and run it. Every video keeps traceability and will not be overwritten.

batch-complete.title: The batch is complete
batch-complete.message: {{completedItems}} of {{itemCount}} results are available. Review the sequence and open any master that needs individual finishing.

mosaic-load.title: Add the mosaic panels
mosaic-load.message: Use captures with compatible overlap and orientation. The assistant will continue through analysis, stacking and stitching.

mosaic-analyze.title: Analyze every panel
mosaic-analyze.message: Zenith measures quality and consistency before stacking to avoid seams with uneven detail.

mosaic-stack.title: Stack the panels
mosaic-stack.message: Confirm the suggested percentage and build a consistent master for every panel before composition.

mosaic-compose.title: Compose and inspect the seams
mosaic-compose.message: Order the panels, validate overlap and create the mosaic. Shared post-processing is available afterward.

mosaic-result.title: The mosaic is stitched
mosaic-result.message: Inspect the seams and open post-processing. History starts from the original mosaic.

deepsky-step.message_0: Add frames and let Zenith group exposure, filter and calibration signature.
deepsky-step.message_1: Review PSF, matches and warnings; incompatible data will not be mixed silently.
deepsky-step.message_2: Start with Auto or a profile and open advanced options only when expert control is needed.
deepsky-step.message_3: The plan is valid. Check the linear outputs and run the integration.
deepsky-step.message_3_blocked: The plan shows a material incompatibility. Open the review and correct it before continuing.

no-source.title: Load a source
no-source.message: Choose a video, sequence or result to begin.

histogram-unavailable.title: 16-bit diagnostics are missing
histogram-unavailable.message: Refresh the measurement before changing levels; this does not modify the image.

needs-analysis.title: Analyze before stacking
needs-analysis.message: Analysis detects quality, motion and the best reference frame.

ready-to-stack.title: Ready to stack
ready-to-stack.message: Review percentage, target and method, then start stacking.

object-finishing-start.title_surface: Choose a lunar or solar finish
object-finishing-start.message_surface: Lunar relief, full-phase and mineral recipes are available; creative recipes stay separate from scientific ones.
object-finishing-start.message_planet: Start with a natural recipe, then tune deconvolution, wavelets and color with A/B.

clipping.title: Protect tonal range
clipping.message: Measured clipping: shadows {{shadow}}% and highlights {{highlight}}%. I can neutralize aggressive levels and compensate the affected extreme.

ringing.title: Reduce halos before sharpening
ringing.message: Artifact analysis measured halos at {{ringing}}. Apply the measured recipe and verify it with A/B.

colour-fringe.title: Review RGB alignment
colour-fringe.message: Measured fringing is {{fringe}}. Zenith can estimate R and B again on the 16-bit master.

low-dynamic-range.title: The signal is compressed
low-dynamic-range.message: About 99.8% of useful signal occupies {{low}}–{{high}}. I can expand it with a safety margin.

dark-result.title: Midtones are very low
dark-result.message: The median is {{median}}%. A {{ev}} EV compensation brings it to a useful reading without moving black.

solar-mono-workflow.title: Is this a mono solar capture?
solar-mono-workflow.message: Useful signal occupies about {{range}}% of the range. If this is the Sun, I can build a conservative H-alpha derivative with curve, false color and noise protection.

solar-filaments.title: Filaments are still neutral
solar-filaments.message: The solar curve is active, but protected filament recovery is still zero. Measure it visually with A/B without altering the master.

tone-curve-opportunity.title: The tone curve is still linear
tone-curve-opportunity.message: I can create a gentle curve from the current histogram to separate shadows, midtones and highlights.

mono-color.title: Protected monochrome path
mono-color.message: RGB colorimetry and atmospheric alignment are locked. For solar data, Solar Lab can create false color without converting or replacing the mono master.

compare-ready.title: You can validate the adjustment
compare-ready.message: Enable A/B and choose Previous step or Original stack; both views preserve zoom and framing.

result-ready.title_continue: Continue one change at a time
result-ready.message_continue: History is active. Adjust one module, compare it and keep only the visible improvement.
result-ready.message_start: Recommended order: levels and curve, detail restoration, noise, then color.

deepsky.pcc_hint: Gaia photometric calibration for broadband OSC/RGB. It uses local indexes and cache before an explicit online fallback; this is not spectrophotometric SPCC.
deepsky.pcc_gate_pending: Eligibility is determined after stacking or combining a linear master.
deepsky.pcc_gate_ready: Available for this broadband RGB master; the recipe remains idempotent.
deepsky.pcc_gate_narrowband: Gaia PCC is invalid for narrowband/dual-band data. Use HOO/SHO or channel combination.
deepsky.pcc_gate_mono: The master is monochrome. Combine LRGB/SHO/HOO first according to your filters.
deepsky.hoo_gate_pending: HOO is enabled only after confirming an OSC Ha+OIII/dual-band master.
deepsky.hoo_gate_ready: Available: OSC Ha+OIII confirmed; HOO creates a derived view only.
deepsky.hoo_gate_unavailable: HOO requires a confirmed OSC Ha+OIII/dual-band master.
deepsky.hoo_gate_sii: HOO does not match SII+OIII. Use an explicit SOO/SHO channel combination.
deepsky.hoo_gate_combined: HOO is not applied again: the master is already a completed channel combination.
deepsky.editor_compare_aria: Comparison between the original master and the current revision
deepsky.editor_crop_body: Drag the frame and its eight handles directly over the image. The view responds immediately; Apply crops SCI, VAR, NEFF, DQ, coverage, and diagnostic maps together.
deepsky.editor_gradient_body: One operation models and subtracts unwanted background. Auto detects clean sky; Point samples lets you edit real measurements. A second extraction can never subtract the nebula twice.
deepsky.editor_gradient_ready: Auto analyses the background, rejects stars and extended signal, and blocks an unstable model. Model and residual remain available for verification.
deepsky.editor_mask_drag: Drag over a nebula or galaxy to protect it
deepsky.editor_astrometry_body: Stacking already tries to validate or solve from the local index. Here you can re-embed validated WCS, provide pointing, or explicitly authorize Gaia online. Pixels never change.
deepsky.editor_color_body: This step is conditional: Gaia PCC balances broadband RGB; mono, dual-band and narrowband data use LRGB/HOO/SHO combinations without inventing missing channels.
deepsky.editor_spcc_gate: SPCC is enabled only with Gaia DR3 XP and a complete instrument profile: camera QE, filters, optics and atmosphere. Without that profile, Zenith offers PCC and never changes the label.
deepsky.editor_deconv_body: Measures valid stars and restores detail with regularized Richardson–Lucy using a circularised global PSF, flux conservation, a reversible pedestal and halo limiting. It does not use the planetary engine or clip to 16-bit.
deepsky.editor_psf_low_confidence: There are not enough valid stars for safe automatic restoration.
deepsky.editor_psf_measure_note: When applied, Zenith measures the PSF on the latest linear revision. If confidence is insufficient, pixels remain unchanged.
deepsky.editor_psf_from_separation: Uses the PSF measured when the layers were created; it is not re-estimated on an already edited branch.
deepsky.editor_manual_psf_confirm: I confirm these widths come from a stellar measurement; they will be recorded as manual values, not as an automatic PSF.
deepsky.editor_manual_psf_required_body: Enter FWHM X/Y measured from stars and enable confirmation. Zenith will not pretend that a low-confidence PSF estimate was measured automatically.
deepsky.editor_branch_only_body: The operation creates a revision only on this branch; the other branch remains unchanged.
deepsky.editor_branch_stretch_body: The preset is adapted again for this branch, not for Combined. The other layer keeps its exact revision until you choose to process and recombine it.
deepsky.editor_branch_finish_body: Finishing affects only this processed branch. You can return to Object or Stars, match their domains, and create Combined when you are satisfied.
deepsky.editor_layers_body: Analyses the PSF and multiscale structure to create Object, Stars, mask and residual layers. Combined remains untouched until you choose to recombine; the original master never changes.
deepsky.editor_not_magic_claim: Verifiable separation, not a promise of perfection
deepsky.editor_layers_truth: The mask lets you audit what was classified as a star. The residual verifies numerical closure and should remain practically zero.
deepsky.editor_edit_object_body: Work on the nebula, galaxy and background without touching the stars. You can return to any tool.
deepsky.editor_edit_stars_body: Reduce size and halos or adjust their colour without altering the object.
deepsky.editor_layer_diagnostics_body: The white mask shows what feeds Stars and helps find halos, missed stars, or misclassified nebulosity. The residual only checks additive closure and should appear almost black.
deepsky.editor_recombine_body: Object + Stars + residual share geometry. Adjust stellar presence or return to either branch without losing its history.
deepsky.editor_recombine_domain_block: Object and Stars must be in the same domain before recombination.
deepsky.editor_layers_low_psf: The PSF did not reach automatic confidence. Review mask and residual before recombining; the original combined image remains untouched.
deepsky.editor_refine_layers_body: Adjust classification after reviewing the mask and residual. Layers are recreated from the linear revision that fed the separator, and branch recipes are replayed transactionally.
deepsky.editor_stretch_body: Each preset is calculated from this master's background, noise, range, and star fraction. Apply creates a non-linear revision; the source FITS remains intact and undoable.
deepsky.editor_branch_detail_body: Multiscale enhancement on this branch before recombination. It preserves the transfer scale, limits noise, and never changes the other layer.
deepsky.editor_detail_needs_stretch: On Combined, this enhancement belongs to the processed output. Complete Stretch or work earlier on Object/Stars.
deepsky.editor_phase_6_body: Opens multiscale noise reduction on a derived revision; the linear master and recipe are not overwritten.
deepsky.editor_phase_7_body: Opens deconvolution and wavelets with star protection, masks and reversible blending.
deepsky.editor_phase_8_body: Opens tone, saturation, contrast and artifact control on the derived image.
deepsky.editor_export_body: Export linear FITS/TIFF and scientific products, or a derived processed image. PNG/JPEG remain presentation-only.
deepsky.view_requires: The "{{view}}" view is only produced when stacking with {{engine}}. This master used a different engine: use Reintegrate and pick that method to produce it.
deepsky.spcc_seed_hint: The FITS header has no RA/Dec or scale. Enter the approximate field centre and your rig's pixel scale.
deepsky.guide_add_lights_detail: Import the session folder; you can then reclassify or remove any frame from Frame groups.
deepsky.guide_strict: Fix the assignment first. If you accept a non-scientific result, Allow degraded continues and records every concession.
deepsky.guide_ready_detail: Review the primary product, linear outputs and destination before running.
deepsky.guide_review_frames_detail: Open Quality to view each light, keep it or discard it reversibly. Nothing is deleted from disk.
deepsky.guide_calibration_detail: Use the highlighted selector. Auto keeps exact matches; a correct flat from another night may require your equipment confirmation.
deepsky.guide_data_detail: Return to Data to remove, reclassify or replace the flagged frames.
deepsky.alert_silence_hint: Hide this warning for this session
deepsky.linker_hint: Link a specific batch to each night's lights, or skip flats/darks for that night. Untick a batch to exclude it entirely. Everything is recorded in the matrix and the recipe.
deepsky.manual_hint: Manual assignment is recorded in the decision matrix and the recipe; the batch choice is your responsibility.
deepsky.proceed_hint: Strict policy blocks on the first contract breach. You can continue in degraded mode: stacking proceeds, every concession is recorded, and the result is flagged as non-scientific where it applies.
deepsky.flat_validation_title: A flat could not be validated
deepsky.flat_validation_missing_white: The header declares neither the white level nor ADC depth, and the pixels did not provide enough evidence to infer them safely. Zenith did not use this frame or publish a partial master.
deepsky.flat_validation_action: You will return to Calibrations. Review that batch or explicitly choose Allow degraded.
deepsky.numeric_guard_summary: A non-finite sample reached a statistical operation that requires a complete numeric ordering.
deepsky.numeric_guard_body: This was not an out-of-memory failure. Zenith stopped the affected branch rather than publish an ambiguous master or close the application.
deepsky.numeric_guard_action: You will return to Stack. The controls remain available and the technical log keeps the exact failure point.
deepsky.calibration_not_applied: Calibration stopped before the lights were integrated.
deepsky.calibration_error_action: You will return to the Calibrations board to correct the highlighted batch. No partial master was published.
deepsky.profile_auto_note: Measures your data (light count, filter, dithering, gradient, background) and sets the optimal recipe; every decision and its reason stay visible in the plan.
deepsky.repeat_integration_hint: Keep frames and registration; revisit only the integration recipe
deepsky.method_blocked_nonlinear: EIDR and NebulaFusion require linear scientific inputs (FITS/TIFF); check the plan warnings.
deepsky.dither_prediction_note: Pre-registration prediction from star offsets; stacking recomputes it with the real registration.
deepsky.pattern_hint: Dithering + robust rejection mitigate banding; check darks/bias from the same session.
deepsky.title: Deep-Sky Stacking
deepsky.hint: Pick your lights and (optional) calibration. Reference, star alignment, satellite rejection and stretch: automatic.
deepsky.step_assistant_0: Add lights; calibration frames are optional. Zenith groups compatible signatures and prevents silent mixing.
deepsky.step_assistant_1: Review grouping, PSF and calibration. Warnings explain exactly what to correct before integration.
deepsky.step_assistant_2: Auto is the recommended starting point. Open advanced controls only when your target needs them.
deepsky.step_assistant_ready: The plan is compatible. Confirm the linear outputs and run it when ready.
deepsky.step_assistant_blocked: Blockers remain. The guide takes you to the exact control that needs correction.
deepsky.step_assistant_empty: Add lights so I can prepare and validate the integration plan.
deepsky.data_intro: Add lights and calibration frames. Zenith groups geometry, Bayer pattern, filter, exposure, gain, binning and temperature.
deepsky.inspect_intro: Review grouping, applicable calibration, incompatibilities and warnings before choosing the recipe.
deepsky.preflight_empty: Add lights to prepare the plan.
deepsky.psf_pending: PSF inspection runs when you enter this step.
deepsky.recipe_intro: Choose a recommended profile. Open advanced options only when you need control over each stage.
deepsky.profile_fast_note: Bilinear, additive normalization and one sigma pass.
deepsky.profile_balanced_note: Lanczos-3, robust scaling and Winsorized rejection.
deepsky.profile_max_note: Winsorized rejection and local normalization; uses more RAM/CPU.
deepsky.multiband_enable: Process every filter in one multiband session
deepsky.multiband_summary: Zenith keeps each integration separate under one shared recipe.
deepsky.multiband_waiting: Shown when Zenith detects two or more spectral profiles.
deepsky.multiband_note_body: {{filters}}. Zenith will run {{count}} separate integrations in one session, extract their lines and keep a shared recipe.
deepsky.fixture_rejection_reason: FWHM and eccentricity are outside the robust range
deepsky.advanced_summary: Advanced options · registration, rejection, normalization, memory and engine
deepsky.tip_capture_mode: Describe the acquisition so compatibility and color products are correct; Auto only classifies frames and never enables EIDR/NebulaFusion.
deepsky.tip_calibration_policy: Strict blocks incompatible metadata or calibration. Allow degraded requires an explicit choice and records every fallback.
deepsky.tip_cosmetic: Removes hot or dead pixels when darks are unavailable.
deepsky.tip_dark_optimization: Scales the master dark to each light to cancel thermal pattern more accurately; requires darks and bias.
deepsky.tip_pedestal: The float32 scientific master preserves negatives and headroom. Add a pedestal only for an external workflow that requires it.
deepsky.tip_manual_darks: Global manual dark assignment. The engine revalidates every signature and never applies an incompatible one.
deepsky.tip_manual_flats: Global manual flat assignment. The engine revalidates every signature and never applies an incompatible one.
deepsky.tip_interpolation: Registration interpolation: Lanczos-3 preserves finer stars; bilinear is smoother and faster.
deepsky.tip_drizzle: Drop-kernel Drizzle for Classic. With EIDR or NebulaFusion, Zenith creates an independent 1× branch and preserves both masters.
deepsky.tip_pixfrac: Drop size: a lower value gives more sharpness but needs more well-dithered frames.
deepsky.tip_eidr_scale: EIDR scale. Auto uses PSF and recoverability; 2× needs at least 12 frames and diverse dithers. Every downgrade is recorded.
deepsky.tip_eidr_mode: Quadratic mode is the scientific reference. Detail uses Huber and is kept only when it improves the holdout.
deepsky.tip_eidr_refine: Refines each translation up to ±0.2 px against the forward model and accepts it only when the holdout improves.
deepsky.tip_cfa_direct: NebulaFusion stacks each CFA photosite in its own channel without demosaic interpolation; preflight requires CFA lights.
deepsky.tip_output_bin: NebulaFusion output scale. Reducing it averages more samples: less noise in exchange for resolution.
deepsky.tip_rejection: Sigma and Average use streaming. Winsorized, median, and percentile use the per-pixel engine; insufficient memory produces an explicit fallback.
deepsky.tip_kappa: Low κ rejects dark outliers and high κ rejects bright ones. Lower is more aggressive; 3.0 is a common balance.
deepsky.tip_clip_iterations: Each κσ iteration recomputes statistics without prior outliers. Auto uses two with six or more frames.
deepsky.tip_normalization: Additive + scale matches level and noise; Additive matches level; Local corrects regions; None preserves input values.
deepsky.tip_auto_crop: Crops partial-coverage borders caused by dithering or rotation.
deepsky.tip_local_weighting: Lucky-DSO weights each region by local stellar sharpness without biasing photometry.
deepsky.tip_gradient_derived: Creates a background model and ABE+SCNR derivative; SCI, VAR, NEFF, and DQ remain linear and untouched.
deepsky.tip_compute_engine: Uses General Settings by default. Expert mode can override it; Auto and Hybrid use the GPU only for stages with scientific parity. GPU only cancels when a required stage is CPU-only.
deepsky.compute_drizzle_cpu: Drizzle keeps scientific integration on CPU
deepsky.compute_sigma_cpu: Iterative sigma keeps scientific integration on CPU
deepsky.compute_tiled_cpu: Tiled/Winsorized/linearfit rejection keeps scientific integration on CPU
deepsky.compute_scientific_cpu: This integration keeps the scientific CPU engine
deepsky.compute_product_cpu: NebulaFusion, STRUCT and EIDR keep scientific integration on CPU
deepsky.compute_gpu_classic: GPU planned: non-iterative Classic integration at 1×
deepsky.compute_gpu_support: GPU planned if validation passes: cosmetic correction and star map; CPU: scientific calibration, registration and models
deepsky.review_intro: Confirm groups, effective method, CPU/GPU per stage and estimated resources. Fallbacks are shown before the run starts.
deepsky.footer_2: choose a profile or advanced options
deepsky.footer_add_lights: add lights to prepare the plan
deepsky.sessions_hint: Each night keeps its lights, signatures, and calibration. Confirmed passed Strict preflight; Candidate still needs validation.
deepsky.dark_flats_header_detected: {{count}} identified from IMAGETYP plus FlatWizard context.
deepsky.scan_signature_note: Zenith will validate each signature before using it.
deepsky.stack_already_running: A stack is already running; wait for it to finish or cancel it.
deepsky.done: Deep-sky stacked. View is auto-stretched; data stays linear for post-processing.
deepsky.keywords_help: Searches names, paths and headers. A time rule such as “2026” automatically creates one group per day.
deepsky.keywords_no_match: The rule does not match any light. Search by name, path, date, filter or camera.
deepsky.method_hint_nf: Each checkbox creates a separate output and adds processing time and disk use; it never changes the other masters. The selector chooses which output opens, remains active and receives the automatic WCS attempt.
deepsky.cfa_direct_hint: Each photosite keeps its own color; requires CFA lights.
deepsky.split_hint: Saves R, G, B and a synthetic L as mono 16-bit TIFF to tweak per channel and recombine (LRGB/SHO).
deepsky.hoo_hint: Derived HOO view of the dual-band master: Ha→R, OIII→G and B (background neutralized). Only the VIEW changes — the linear float32 master (SCI/VAR/NEFF/DQ) stays intact; Reintegrate or switch views to return to the original RGB.
deepsky.spcc_hint: Photometric color calibration against Gaia DR3 (broadband OSC/RGB, needs internet). For narrowband/dual-band use HOO/SHO.
deepsky.no_base: No destination folder to export to.
deepsky.expert_recipe_saved_body: The recipe did not change when returning to Essential. Open Expert only if you want to edit its parameters.
deepsky.expert_recipe_edit_hint: Switch to Expert to edit it
deepsky.session_quality_hint: Measured linear masters and metrics, not the STF view.
deepsky.review_no_blockers: No blockers; the contract is ready.
deepsky.review_outputs_body: Linear master and reproducible recipe; SCI/VAR/NEFF/DQ when the plan is scientifically eligible.
deepsky.review_parallel_outputs: {{masters}} separate masters will be created: {{groups}} integration group(s) × {{products}} branches. They start from the same lights and calibration decisions; each branch runs its own sampling, integration and export.
deepsky.review_technical: View technical plan, signatures and fallbacks
deepsky.calibration_matrix_truncated: Showing 50 of {{count}}; the recipe preserves every decision.
deepsky.frame_open_hint: Click to view the stretched frame and its reason
deepsky.psf_inspection_hint: Click a row to view the stretched frame and its reason. Discard removes it from the plan and stack reversibly; the final decision is recomputed from the complete calibrated data.
deepsky.frame_reason_ok: No observations: metrics are within the batch
deepsky.viewer_stretch_hint: View stretch (STF). Does not modify the stacking data.
deepsky.viewer_balance_hint: Neutralizes the background per channel (removes the linear OSC green cast), view only.
deepsky.inspecting_frames: Measuring stars, PSF/FWHM, noise and eccentricity…
deepsky.reading_headers: Reading headers and preparing the plan…
deepsky.scan_folder_hint: Reads IMAGETYP; folders and names are safe fallbacks
deepsky.folder_created: Folder created and opened; you can now confirm it.
deepsky.folder_instruction_source: One click opens a folder. Nothing is selected until you press “Use this folder”.
deepsky.folder_instruction_destination: One click opens a folder. Nothing is selected until you press “Save here”.
deepsky.folder_error_hint: That path could not be opened. Go up one level or use the system picker.
deepsky.guide_refreshing_detail: Zenith is recalculating groups, calibration and eligibility from the current selection. Previous messages are no longer considered valid.
deepsky.work_dir_choose_hint: Click to choose where caches, masters and exports are stored
deepsky.work_dir_change_hint: Click to change the working and output folder
deepsky.frame_groups_hint: Lights are required; calibration is optional and validated by signature.
deepsky.plan_scale_note: Darks from a different exposure were found. They will not be accepted or scaled unless the backend validates pedestal state, absence of amp glow, linearity, correlation, and residual.
deepsky.plan_dark_flat_note: Dark-flats do not match the flat exposure. Strict policy will block incompatible calibration.
deepsky.plan_candidate_note: ? = candidate by name/filter/exposure. Only the Strict preflight matrix confirms scientific compatibility.
deepsky.drag_hint: Drag a file to another category to reclassify it; use Remove to discard it.
deepsky.prog_edit_hint: Each module creates a derived revision with exact undo, redo, and A/B.
deepsky.prog_reference_alt: Reference light stretched for viewing only
deepsky.prog_reference_registered_alt: Reference light adjusted to the master geometry
deepsky.prog_reference_registered_label: BEFORE · reference in the same framing
deepsky.prog_reference_alignment_unavailable: Could not align the reference to the master crop
deepsky.prog_visual_preparing_note: Comparison activates when the engine publishes a real view.
deepsky.prog_wait_master_note: The right side will show only an output published by the engine.
deepsky.prog_view_failed: That scientific view is unavailable for the active product. SCI remains selected.
deepsky.prog_compare_sync_aria: Synchronized comparison between the reference light and the current master
deepsky.prog_compare_reset_title: Double-click or press here to reset the framing
deepsky.prog_compare_help: Wheel to zoom. Drag to move both images together. Double-click to reset. Use plus, minus, arrow keys, or Home from the keyboard.
deepsky.prog_complete_body: Linear master published. Processing will create derived revisions only.
deepsky.export_hint: Saved to your work folder (or next to your lights if none is set). The stretch uses the current mode/intensity.
deepsky.combine_desc: Assign linear MONO FITS/TIFF masters. They are registered and combined without destructive gradient removal, SCNR, or stretching; the view uses a temporary STF only.
deepsky.combine_sho: SHO — Hubble (SII→R · Ha→G · OIII→B · no SCNR)
deepsky.combine_need: Assign at least channels R, G and B (or Ha/OIII).
deepsky.combine_done: Channels combined. Adjust the stretch in the bottom bar.
deepsky.auto_crop_note: At the end, the border frame with fewer overlapping frames (dithering/rotation) is cropped. Turn it off to keep the full framing, with noisier edges.
deepsky.local_weighting_note: Each sky region is stacked preferring the frames where THAT region came out sharpest (local seeing). Zenith exclusive: traditional stackers only weight whole frames.
deepsky.work_dir_hint: Next to the lights; choose another disk for caches, masters and exports
deepsky.work_dir_pick: Working & output folder (caches, masters and exports)
deepsky.advisor_reco_superres: Recommended scale: {{scale}} — super-resolution candidate once EIDR is available
deepsky.wbpp_hint: One row per night, filter and exposure. You can link flats, darks, dark-flats and bias; Auto lets the signature decide. If a correct flat is from another night, Zenith asks for explicit confirmation only for missing identity fields.
deepsky.scan_accumulates: You can scan more folders: they add to the previous ones. Use Remove on a group to empty it.
deepsky.calibrations_intro: Zenith proposes exact and reusable signatures. You only need to review flagged rows; a forced signature is never disguised as compatible.
deepsky.calibrations_essential_body: Leave Auto when the state is Exact. Use a validated reusable batch to share flats across nights; unsafe choices disable scientific engines.
deepsky.quality_step_intro: Keep the quick recommendation or open the expert diagnostic to inspect PSF, noise, roundness and reference selection.
deepsky.quality_essential_title: What to keep and what to review
deepsky.quality_essential_body: Zenith never silently discards a doubtful frame: it flags it, explains why and lets you open it before deciding.
deepsky.verify_scientific_title: Confirm this flat as scientifically equivalent
deepsky.verify_scientific_body: I confirm the camera/sensor, read mode, ROI, ADC and optical train did not change between nights. Zenith will still block any measurable geometry, gain/ISO, offset, binning, CFA, filter or batch-stability mismatch.
deepsky.verify_scientific_confirm: This is a scientific attestation: you confirm camera/sensor, read mode, ROI, ADC and optical train did not change between nights. Zenith still verifies geometry, gain/ISO, offset, binning, CFA, filter and flat stability. Any failure keeps the batch blocked. Confirm?
deepsky.apply_compatible_pick: First choose a batch in one row; then you can apply it to compatible nights.
deepsky.apply_compatible_done: Assignment applied to {{count}} compatible night(s); the backend will revalidate every light.
deepsky.force_unsafe_confirm: This batch does not match the preliminary signature. Zenith will record it as unsafe, will not apply it as scientific calibration, and will disable NebulaFusion/EIDR. Keep this choice for audit?
deepsky.force_global_confirm: The global override will be revalidated per light. Incompatible signatures will not be applied and will downgrade NF/EIDR to Classic. Keep this selection?
deepsky.file_search: Search by name, path or filter…
deepsky.footer_3: choose the method and its products
deepsky.step_assistant_3: Auto is the recommended starting point. Expert opens full control without changing the recipe by itself.
deepsky.product_classic_hint: Creates the most compatible and stable linear master. It is the safe processing reference.
deepsky.product_nf_hint: Creates another linear master for faint signal, with noise and coverage maps. It does not mix with or replace Classic.
deepsky.product_struct_hint: Creates a separate validated structure layer. It computes NebulaFusion Full as a dependency; it is not a combined master.
deepsky.product_eidr_hint: Creates an independent higher-resolution reconstruction only where PSF, SNR and dithering provide evidence.
deepsky.primary_product_hint: Remains active for editing/quick export and receives the automatic WCS attempt; it does not change pixels.
deepsky.product_shared_run: same lights and calibration decisions; separate integration; no pixel mixing
deepsky.product_opens: will open and attempt WCS solving
deepsky.product_struct_with_nf: STRUCT uses its own NebulaFusion Full pass; the selected NebulaFusion output is also preserved.
deepsky.product_struct_hidden_dependency: STRUCT will compute NebulaFusion Full internally, but only STRUCT is exposed as a selected output.
deepsky.product_drizzle_conflict: Drizzle creates a separate Classic branch; NebulaFusion/STRUCT/EIDR keep an internal 1× grid.
deepsky.product_parallel_shared: They start from the same lights and calibration decisions; each branch runs its own grid, integration and export.
deepsky.product_parallel_auto_classic: Classic was added automatically because Drizzle applies only to that output.
deepsky.product_branch_struct: STRUCT · internal NebulaFusion Full · internal 1× drizzle
deepsky.products_compatibility_title: How products coexist and which parameters they share
deepsky.products_shared: Common base: accepted/rejected lights and calibration decisions. Zenith reuses compatible caches when the grid allows it.
deepsky.products_separate: Separate: each engine integrates its own output; Classic, NebulaFusion and EIDR pixels are never mixed automatically.
deepsky.products_parameters: Parameters: Classic uses rejection and its own Drizzle; NebulaFusion uses mode/binning; STRUCT always uses NebulaFusion Full; EIDR uses scale/solver/micro-registration. Scientific branches use an internal 1× grid and publish their own output scale.
deepsky.target_type_hint: Normal keeps star registration. Comet creates Stars, Comet, and Combined layers.
deepsky.comet_pending: Detect and confirm the nucleus in the first, middle, and last frame.
deepsky.comet_registered_note: Coordinates use the star-registered grid. Correct them in the row and confirm the nucleus.
deepsky.comet_low_confidence: The trajectory still has low confidence; review the coordinates.
deepsky.comet_need_lights: Add at least five lights with DATE-OBS for a robust trajectory fit.
deepsky.comet_detecting: Registering samples and searching for motion…
deepsky.editor_curves_body: Adjust the master, luminance, and channel curves independently. Selective saturation works by hue while protecting luminance.
deepsky.editor_curves_mono_body: Mono enables only the master and luminance curves. Zenith does not invent RGB, hue, or saturation.
deepsky.editor_curve_canvas: Curve editor; click to add a point, drag to adjust, and right-click to remove
deepsky.editor_curves_ready: The identity curve changes no pixels. Adjust only what is needed.
deepsky.editor_curves_applied: Curves applied as a reproducible revision.
deepsky.editor_curves_need_stretch: Curves and HSL belong to the presentation output. Complete Stretch or work on an already stretched branch.
deepsky.editor_palette_analyzing_body: Every preview uses the same STF, geometry, and linear masters for an honest comparison.
deepsky.editor_annotation_body: Zenith projects the catalog through the master's WCS and creates an independent transparent layer. Annotations never alter scientific pixels.
deepsky.editor_annotation_needs_wcs: Annotations require a validated WCS. Return to Astrometry; lack of network access never modifies or blocks the master.
deepsky.close_result_bar_hint: Minimize this bar; you can restore it with “View master” in the header.
deepsky.editor_add_channel_masters_fixture: Interactive fixture: this opens the LRGB/HOO/SHO combiner. In the native app you can choose linear mono masters without modifying their source files.
deepsky.editor_allow_unstable_gradient: Allow unstable model (recorded in the recipe)
deepsky.editor_analysis_pending: Analyzing the master to adapt the presets…
deepsky.editor_annotation_fixture_export: Interactive fixture: the native app can save either the transparent PNG overlay or the composite annotated image.
deepsky.editor_astrometry_catalog_missing: No local Gaia mosaic is available for this field. You can authorize online Gaia access or install the file shown below.
deepsky.editor_astrometry_needs_seed: RA, Dec, or image scale is missing from the headers. Provide them to locate the field.
deepsky.editor_astrometry_retry: The master was not changed; retry or use the local mosaic.
deepsky.editor_astrometry_timeout: Gaia did not respond in time
deepsky.editor_channel_combiner_unavailable: Publish the mono master first, or return to the result view to open the LRGB/HOO/SHO combiner.
deepsky.editor_color_broadband_body: Gaia PCC uses stars and the WCS to balance broadband RGB. It is idempotent and preserves the original.
deepsky.editor_color_mono_body: A single mono master does not contain the other channels. Add L/R/G/B or narrowband channels; Zenith will not invent color.
deepsky.editor_color_skip_body: This source is already combined or cannot be classified safely. You can skip this step and preserve the linear branch.
deepsky.editor_confirm_linear_tiff: Confirm that this TIFF contains linear 16/32-bit data from a scientific master. Zenith will detect known signs of stretching, but a TIFF without metadata cannot prove linearity mathematically.
deepsky.editor_confirm_replace_session: Opening another master will replace the session and its in-memory browsable products. Existing FITS/TIFF files will not be deleted or modified. Continue?
deepsky.editor_crop_overlay: Editable crop area. Arrow keys move it; Shift plus arrow keys use larger steps.
deepsky.editor_crop_safe_body: The same rectangle is applied to SCI, scientific maps, Object, Stars, mask, and residual. Zenith recreates safe branches and remeasures WCS, gradient, and PSF when they depend on geometry; the source master remains intact.
deepsky.editor_curves_pending: Curve modified · Apply creates a reproducible revision.
deepsky.editor_detail_body: Multiscale enhancement constrained by the noise floor and stellar luminance. Strength decreases automatically in bright cores.
deepsky.editor_dualband_body: Zenith separates or reunites the available channels and generates previews with the same STF. Choosing a card only changes the view; Apply creates a derived linear revision.
deepsky.editor_finish_body: Adjust saturation and contrast on the current revision while automatically reducing the effect on stars and bright cores.
deepsky.editor_finish_needs_stretch: Finishing is optional and becomes available only after stretching. The linear output remains available.
deepsky.editor_missing_component_masters: The session was identified as multiband, but did not publish the required Ha/OIII/SII masters. Reintegrate while preserving scientific components.
deepsky.editor_missing_independent_channels: Only one active mono master is available. Filter labels describe its signal, but do not create independent Ha/OIII/SII planes.
deepsky.editor_mono_channels_body: This mono master contains one measured channel. Add the remaining Ha/OIII/SII or L/R/G/B masters; Zenith will neither separate absent spectral lines nor invent color.
deepsky.editor_multifilter_body: Zenith registers Ha, SII, and both OIII signals; reconciles their scale, noise, PSF, and coverage; and combines OIII robustly before creating comparable palettes.
deepsky.editor_noise_body: Filters linear noise with a robust neighborhood and limits blending where structure is present. It does not open the planetary module or convert data to 16-bit.
deepsky.editor_oiii_pending: Before palettes are shown, both OIII signals will be validated and reconciled. Neither will be chosen silently.
deepsky.editor_oiii_reconciled: Duplicate OIII reconciled and validated; both nights/filters contribute according to noise and overlap.
deepsky.editor_palette_not_pcc: Broadband PCC does not apply to this signal. Palettes are interpretive and preserve the linear channels.
deepsky.editor_palette_stale: Preview is stale; recalculate the gallery before applying it.
deepsky.editor_pcc_needs_wcs: Complete Astrometry first: PCC needs to know which stars it is measuring.
deepsky.editor_samples_aria: Background samples. Click to add a sample or toggle the nearest one. Use arrow keys and Space with the keyboard.
deepsky.editor_samples_tip: Click to add or disable contaminated points; protected areas are never sampled.
deepsky.editor_source_preserved_body: Undo, Reset, and A/B are rebuilt from the immutable source master. The annotation layer is only a publication product.
deepsky.editor_spcc_question: Why is this not called SPCC?
deepsky.editor_state_unavailable: The active session could not be validated. The master was not modified; retry before opening another file.
deepsky.prog_product_fallback: Validation failed; the indicated safe output was preserved
deepsky.result_protected: Protected linear master · edits are revisions

milkyway.editor_missing_primary: The engine published neither Composite nor Sky. The remaining maps were preserved, but Studio has no scientific image to open.
milkyway.editor_crop_resets_edits: Synchronized crop creates new linear geometry for Sky, Ground, Composite, and maps. Current editing revisions will not be copied; the originals and their recipe remain intact. Continue?
milkyway.editor_crop_safe_body: Every available product is published through staging and shares one new geometryId. Original FITS files are never overwritten; when WCS is valid, CRPIX moves to the new origin.
milkyway.header_body: Moving sky, fixed ground, and editable layers.
milkyway.assistant_body: Zenith will preserve the geometry and recipe as you continue.
milkyway.data_title: What do you want to preserve?
milkyway.data_body: Zenith registers the sky without dragging the ground. The recommended option also preserves separate layers and an editable composition.
milkyway.mode_freeze_body: Composes the horizon and preserves auditable Sky, Ground, Mask, Composite, and maps.
milkyway.mode_layers_body: Delivers Sky, Ground, Mask, and Composite.
milkyway.mode_sky_body: Registers the entire frame with the stars and creates no ground branch.
milkyway.linear_input_notice: Import linear FITS/TIFF. Develop camera RAW files outside Zenith until a scientifically validated RAW reader is available.
milkyway.unify_exposure_body: Only when ISO/gain or exposure changed; the concession is recorded.
milkyway.mask_body: Auto proposes the boundary. Correct it with the horizon or brush and confirm: the same mask governs registration, composition, crop, and editing.
milkyway.mask_image_alt: Base frame used to define sky and ground
milkyway.mask_empty: Add frames to create the mask.
milkyway.mask_native_preview_alt: Exact soft mask calculated by the engine
milkyway.mask_confirm_body: Prevents double edges, ghost trees, and sky over the ground.
milkyway.mask_sky_only_body: Zenith registers every pixel with the stars. This mode does not request a ground boundary or confirmation.
milkyway.mask_sky_only_ready: No boundary is pending. Returning to Sharp sky + ground requires detecting and confirming a new mask.
milkyway.registration_body: The sky uses stars; the ground remains on the base frame. Zenith composes distortion and registration before a single resampling pass.
milkyway.radial_requires_distortion: Ultra-wide includes radial correction. Choose Auto, Affine, or Homography to turn it off.
milkyway.integration_title: Integrate without erasing stars or landscape
milkyway.integration_body: Rejection is measured per branch. Aircraft, satellites, and hot pixels are excluded from the sky without turning foliage or water into smears.
milkyway.preset_quality_body: Two passes · edges and fine noise
milkyway.dynamic_pixels_body: Complements darks; does not replace them.
milkyway.fallback_strict_body: An unreliable frame or branch stops the job before publication.
milkyway.fallback_degraded_body: Zenith may exclude failed frames; every concession is shown and the result is marked non-scientific.
milkyway.composition_body: The confirmed mask and a soft transition combine both branches. Zenith publishes the composite together with Sky, Ground, and every map for later audit or editing.
milkyway.product_composite_body: Linear blend with an auditable boundary
milkyway.keep_layers_body: Sky, Ground, Composite, Mask, and maps always remain available for auditing and editing.
milkyway.sky_only_products_body: Publishes the sky master, full-frame mask, variance, coverage, rejection, and reproducible recipe.
milkyway.publish_body: The original and linear layers remain immutable. The editor processes the Composite while keeping Sky, Ground, and Mask as synchronized comparison sources.
milkyway.open_editor_body: Edit the Composite; inspect Sky, Ground, and Mask without altering them.
milkyway.health_ready: Ready to continue · no pending decisions.
milkyway.progress_body: Zenith preserves the linear layers while it works.
milkyway.active_run_body: Closing must not abandon or confuse the active job. Keep this view open or let the safe process continue in the background.
milkyway.dialog_output: Milky Way working and output folder
milkyway.preparing_body: Validating frames, geometry, and working space.
milkyway.fixture_summary: Layers, variance, coverage, rejection, and recipe published per branch.
milkyway.cancel_requested: Cancellation requested; safely closing the partial product.
milkyway.reason_two_lights: Add at least two night-sky frames.
milkyway.reason_unreadable_files: Some included files cannot be read; remove or deselect them.
milkyway.reason_four_lights: Freeze Ground and robust rejection require at least four frames.
milkyway.reason_base_frame: Choose a base frame included in the session.
milkyway.reason_geometry: Included frames do not share geometry and channels.
milkyway.reason_exposure: Frames use different exposure or ISO/gain; enable Unify exposure or split the batch.
milkyway.reason_exposure_warning: Unify exposure will normalize the batch and record the concession.
milkyway.reason_dark_mismatch: Known darks do not match the lights' exposure, ISO/gain, or geometry.
milkyway.reason_flat_mismatch: Known flats do not match the lights' ISO/gain, geometry, or channels.
milkyway.reason_dark_metadata: Darks have incomplete metadata: Strict will require native validation before calibration.
milkyway.reason_flat_metadata: Flats have incomplete metadata: Strict will require native validation before calibration.
milkyway.reason_mask_required: Freeze Ground needs a sky/ground mask.
milkyway.reason_mask_confirm: Confirm the mask to protect the horizon and foreground.
milkyway.reason_mask_confidence: The automatic mask has low confidence; correct it with the horizon or brush.
milkyway.reason_registration_model: The registration model is not valid.
milkyway.reason_registration_sky: Sky star registration has not been validated.
milkyway.reason_registration_inliers: Registration does not retain enough control stars.
milkyway.reason_registration_rms: The registration residual exceeds the configured limit.
milkyway.reason_registration_ground: The fixed-ground branch has not been validated.
milkyway.reason_single_resample: Transforms must be composed before one resampling pass.
milkyway.reason_robust_integration: Use sigma or Winsorized rejection to suppress aircraft, satellites, and dynamic pixels.
milkyway.reason_allow_degraded: AllowDegraded may exclude failed frames and marks the result as non-scientific.
milkyway.reason_transition_range: The sky/ground transition must be between 0 and 512 px.
milkyway.reason_foreground_frame: Add at least one foreground frame or use the stacked/base ground.
milkyway.reason_output: Choose a working and output folder.
milkyway.reason_publish: Choose at least one output or open the editor.
